summary: Ramón Prats is a tibetologist who held posts at Pompeu Fabra University and Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources.
Randall Studstill works in religious studies and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Richard K. Payne until circa 2002 and under teacher Steven D. Goodman until circa 2002.

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (c. 2003–2008). He studied under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin, co-supervisor Kakkapalliye Anuruddha, and traditional teacher Attaragama Gnanawimala.

Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under Tai Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, the 13th Dalai Lama, Kalu Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught numerous prominent students.

Raniero Gnoli (1930–2025) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giuseppe Tucci from circa 1950 to 1954. He held a post at Sapienza University of Rome from circa 1964 to 2000.

Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh (1897–1982) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at Fergusson College and under Sukhlal Sanghvi, he served as Professor of Sanskrit and Ancient Indian History at Gujarat Vidyapith and Secretary at Gujarat Puratattva Mandir (c. 1920–1930).

Rasmus Rask (1787–1832) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (c. 1807–1811) and later served there as Professor of Literary History and Librarian from circa 1825 to 1832.

Ravindra Singh Bisht (born 1944) is a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Lucknow. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from circa 2003 to 2004.
Rawi Bhavilai (1925–2017) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Adelaide. He served as Director at Chulalongkorn University from circa 1945 to 1986.
Raymond D. Fogelson (1933–2020) studied at Wesleyan University (c. 1951–1955) and the University of Pennsylvania (c. 1956–1962). He held a post at the University of Chicago from circa 1965 to 2010.

Rebecca Redwood French works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned degrees at the University of Washington and Yale University, later holding posts as Associate of Law at the University of Colorado Boulder (c. 1991–2001) and Professor of Law at University at Buffalo.

Regbi Pubaev (1928–1991) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at St. Petersburg University (c. 1947–1952). He held posts at Buryat State University (c. 1955–1958) and the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies (c. 1958–1991).

Reginald A. Ray (born 1942) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Mircea Eliade and Chögyam Trungpa. His career includes posts as Professor in Buddhist Studies at Naropa University and teacher at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Rei Yoshimura (1929–2013) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University (c. 1949–1953). He later served as a professor at Waseda University from circa 1973 to 2000.

Reiko Ohnuma (born 1964) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at UC Berkeley and the University of Michigan, she held posts at UT Austin and the University of Alabama, joining Dartmouth College's faculty in circa 1999.

Reimon Yuki (1902–1992) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (c. 1924–1927). He later served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (c. 1953–1963) and held posts at Ryukoku and Kyoto Women's universities.
Reiner Wiehl (1929–2010) was a philosopher who held academic posts at the University of Hamburg from circa 1971 to 1977 and at Heidelberg University from circa 1977 to 1997.
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at the Free University of Berlin and the Göttingen State and University Library (circa 1991).
Reinhold Klotz (1807–1870) was a scholar in linguistics who studied at Leipzig University from circa 1825 to 1829. He subsequently held an academic post at Leipzig University from circa 1832 to 1870.

Reinhold Rost (1822–1896) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Jena. He served at The King's School Canterbury, St Augustine's College, the Royal Asiatic Society, and as Librarian for the India Office and its library.
